correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=3 and conjugate p,q in [1,infinity], the boundary arcs and straight segment lengths yield the exact loss function F(alpha,beta). Its derivative factors as 2 sin(beta/2)[(p+q)sin(beta/2)-q tan(alpha)cos(beta/2)], giving a unique optimum at beta=min(alpha,2 arctan(tan(alpha)/p)), with properly treated p=1 and infinite endpoints. Closed-form substitution gives the reported minimum. The second alpha-derivative has a strictly positive prefactor and polynomial H(p,s), whose threshold value H(1+s,s)=2s(2-s)(s+1)^2>=0 for 1<s<=2 and which increases in p. This proves strict real-order convexity via G_n"=2pi^2 f"/n^3, and monotonicity. Jensen bounds for nested n-gons and strict optimal crossing prove the unrestricted nonnesting obstruction. The included standard-library checker passed 1094 finite checks and is supplemental.

value.rationale: The work resolves a natural weight-dependent regular-family specialization of an explicit published open Dowker-type perimeter-deviation question, with a sharp inscribed-to-crossing boundary p=1+sec(pi/n), a complete unique-radius profile, strict order convexity, and a new rigorous implication for all convex n-gons: above the threshold neither wholly inside nor wholly outside polygons can be optimal. This is a mathematically motivated classification and phase transition, not a mere low-order computation or a claim of global unrestricted optimization.
risks: No determination of unrestricted optimizer or necessary nonnesting threshold.
The profile is confined to a fixed regular symmetry family for exact optimization.
